title: A Personal Academic Statement Using Perfect Tenses
writingModel: I have been interested in the relationship between language and identity since I first encountered the concept in my second year at WKU. Since then, my interest has grown from a passing curiosity into what I believe is a genuine research vocation.

Over the past three years, I have studied linguistics, discourse analysis, and sociolinguistics at undergraduate level. I have completed all required modules with distinction and have been consistently ranked among the top students in my cohort. I have also attended three national conferences and have presented my work at two of them.

My research focus has been developing throughout this period. I have been particularly interested in code-switching — the practice of alternating between languages within a conversation — among Kazakhstani university students. I have interviewed 24 students for my ongoing thesis project, and I have been analysing the patterns that have emerged from these conversations for the past six months.

Through this work, I have discovered that language choice in Kazakhstani academic contexts is far more strategic than it appears on the surface. I have learned that students switch languages not randomly but in response to topic, audience, and social relationship. I have developed a framework for understanding these patterns that I believe contributes to the broader literature on multilingualism in post-Soviet educational settings.

I have also been developing my professional skills alongside my research. I have worked as a teaching assistant for two semesters, during which I have supported over 40 students with their academic writing. I have found this experience invaluable: it has deepened my understanding of how students acquire academic language, which has in turn enriched my research perspective.

In applying for this programme, I bring a strong foundation in linguistic theory, a completed data collection phase, and several months of active analysis. I have read widely in the field and have engaged critically with the key debates. I believe I am ready to take the next step. What I have been building over these three years has prepared me for it.
